items.fact: Dropout: drop each neuron independently with probability p each training step
items.where: Section 4, first paragraph; PyTorch convention box

items.fact: Dropout: authors suggest keep probability around 0.8 for hidden layers
items.where: CORRECTED in a visible box (section 4): Srivastava et al. recommend retention 0.5 for hidden units (range 0.5 to 0.8, Appendix A.4) and 0.8 for real-valued inputs

items.fact: Dropout prevents co-adaptation: no neuron can rely on one specific partner; redundant, robust features
items.where: Section 4, first paragraph

items.fact: Dropout is equivalent to training an implicit ensemble of subnetworks
items.where: Section 4, first paragraph; Dropout as an ensemble tab

items.fact: Train vs inference scaling: inference drops nothing, activations scaled so the expected value matches
items.where: Section 4, Train against inference; dropout animation

items.fact: Original scheme: at inference multiply activations by keep probability
items.where: Section 4 list; animation mode 'Original scheme'

items.fact: Inverted dropout: at training divide surviving activations by keep probability; inference is a plain forward pass; what frameworks do
items.where: Section 4 list; animation mode 'Inverted dropout'

items.fact: Dropout largely absent from modern LLM pretraining (single-epoch data means little overfitting) but common in fine-tuning and smaller models
items.where: Section 4, 'Where dropout is used now' table and closing sentence (PaLM, T5 1.1, nanoGPT sourced); section 8

items.fact: Data augmentation: random but realistic transforms (flips, rotations, crops, noise) enlarge and diversify the training set
items.where: Section 5, first paragraph; augmentation widget

items.fact: Augmentation attacks overfitting at the data level; the highest-leverage fix when feasible
items.where: Section 5, first paragraph; 'What each buys' (Zhang et al. Table 1: crops 3.5 points, weight decay at most 0.3)

items.fact: Early stopping: monitor validation loss; stop before the model starts overfitting
items.where: Section 6

items.fact: Early stopping: free, always on; keep the best-validation checkpoint
items.where: Section 6

items.fact: Weight decay: penalise large weights so the model captures patterns rather than memorising
items.where: Section 3, first sentence

items.fact: Weight decay two implementations: L2 in the loss (λ/2)||w||², penalty enters the gradient and flows through the optimiser
items.where: Section 3, list item 1

items.fact: Decoupled weight decay: w ← w − ηλw alongside the gradient step
items.where: Section 3, list item 2

items.fact: For plain SGD the two coincide
items.where: Section 3 (Loshchilov and Hutter Proposition 1, up to rescaling λ by the learning rate)

items.fact: For Adam they do not: L2 divided by the second-moment term, so weights with large gradients barely decayed
